news.title: 融资、人工智能及其他法官与律师事务
news.snippet: 探讨法律界在AI时代的funding趋势与bench-bar业务新动态，解析司法与律师行业智能化转型。
news.raw_snippet: Email this postLike this postShare this post on LinkedIn. We’ve said before that plaintiff lawyers do a better job of putting together bench-bar conferences than the defense side does. It is not just us saying that. Last week, we were at a bench-bar conference focused on Multidistrict Litigations (MDLs), and a state court judge told us the same thing. That judge was just one of many important judges (from state courts, including the Texas Business Court, as well as federal district and circuit courts) who came together to discuss the latest doings in MDLs, which have become the 64,000 pound gorilla of the American civil docket. Also in attendance were luminaries of the plaintiff bar, the usual suspects among defense hackery, and, increasingly important, tech vendors (more about artificial intelligence (AI) in a bit) and a banker (more about third party litigation funding (TPLF) in a bit. Also on the panel was a federal judge who had terrified us in a particular case.

news.raw_snippet: # SpaceX: The AI IPO Wearing a Spacesuit. Make no mistake: the anticipated debut of SpaceX is an AI IPO wearing a spacesuit. For that, the company is expected to spend over $300 billion in capital expenditures by the end of the decade. For investors looking to capture this infrastructure boom without taking on single-stock concentration risk, the ROBO Global Artificial Intelligence ETF (THNQ B-) offers a structural approach. Outfitting a mammoth data center like xAI’s Colossus to a gigawatt scale requires a massive volume of processors and memory architecture. While the winner of the AI software wars won’t be known for some time, semiconductor designers like Advanced Micro Devices and connectivity leaders like Astera Labs stand to collect a toll on every ounce of compute capacity that SpaceX must deploy to scale up its operations. The ultimate mission, after all, remains making humanity a “spacefaring civilization.” For investors seeking exposure to this physical side of SpaceX, the ROBO Global Robotics and Automation Index (ROBO) serves as a targeted vehicle.

news.title: 随着AI工具能力增强，雇佣人工智能是否成为新趋势
news.snippet: 探讨企业是否应直接hiring AI系统替代传统人力，AI capability跃升推动recruitment模式革新。
news.raw_snippet: Just a few years ago, businesses looking to build AI-powered products had little choice but to hire artificial intelligence engineers with deep expertise in machine learning, data science, model training, and deployment. This raises an interesting question: **As AI becomes easier to access, does that increase the value of AI engineers—or make them less essential for businesses building new products?**. I don’t think the answer to your question is black or white. I think that it is possible you could answer your own question. For example, if you are a CTO and you have an existing staff of software engineers, what would you do if you want to build new AI solutions into existing applications or build entirely new applications? You could hire new AI IT staff, get your current staff trained, hire AI IT consultants, or a combination thereof. As time marches on, it is entirely possible that you would want to trim your IT staff.

news.title: AI如何助力中小企业招聘更优人才
news.snippet: 美国US Chamber of Commerce发布指南，阐述AI技术帮助small businesses优化talent acquisition，提升招聘精准度。
news.raw_snippet: Practical and real-world advice on how to run your business — from managing employees to keeping the books. # How AI Can Help Small Business Owners **Overcome Hiring Challenges**. A third of U.S. small business owners and entrepreneurs worry about choosing the wrong candidate, according to LinkedIn data. Here’s how the technology can help and how small business employers are using AI to find qualified candidates. More small business owners and entrepreneurs report feeling added pressure to make the right hiring decisions these days, according to LinkedIn. Nearly 35% of small business owners said they worry about missing out on a top-notch candidate or choosing the wrong candidates, and 52% said they’d previously hired someone who didn’t work out. ## How AI can help with hiring. Generative AI tools, such as ChatGPT, can help write job descriptions and job advertisements based on the characteristics you’ve outlined for the open role and the ideal candidate.
